description.narrative: Projektet syftar till att stödja behoven hos den konfliktdrabbade befolkningen i östra Ukraina, som led av den ryska federationens militära aggression. Projektet kommer i synnerhet att stärka lokala myndigheters och medborgares efterlevnad av de tolv principerna för god förvaltning, som utgör den oumbärliga ramen för att uppnå det gemensamma bästa för lokalsamhällen, inklusive när det gäller förbättring av tjänster (i detta sammanhang kommer projektet att fokusera om miljöskydd och sociala tjänster).

The project aims to support the needs of conflict effected population in Eastern Ukraine, who suffered from the military aggression of the Russian Federation. In particular, the Project will strengthen adherence by local governments and citizens to the twelve principles of Good Governance, which constitute the indispensable framework to achieve the Common Good of local communities, including in terms of service improvement (in this context, the Project will focus on environmental protection and social services).

The proposed Project aims at strengthening adherence by local governments and citizens to the twelve principles of Good Governance, which constitute the indispensable framework to achieve the Common Good of local communities, including in terms of service improvement (in this context, the Project will focus on environmental protection and social services). The notion of Common Good refers to what is shared and beneficial for all members of a given community, including the most vulnerable. It also refers to what is achieved by citizenship, collective action, and active participation in the realm of politics and public service.

sector.narrative: Civilian peace-building, conflict prevention and resolution

description.narrative:
Before the Russian military invasion, the Project was intended to work in the government-controlled areas of Donetsk and Luhansk oblasts. As the war intensified, many settlements in the east of Ukraine became an area of active military fighting and relentless shelling. Due to an uncertain situation and devastating war casualties, the projects core activities were put on hold until the condition stabilised and became more predictable. In 2023, the project mainly focused on the emergency response activities and needs assessment and discussions with local authorities to ensure an evidence-based response to be rolled out. Given this, the geographic targeting of the Project has been revised. As a result, a new, more flexible and responsive geographic coverage framework was developed, which envisages the expansion to the neighbouring war-affected and liberated areas of Chernihiv, Dnipropetrovsk, Mykolaiv and Sumy oblasts. Moreover, the Project is delivered via an area-based approach, whereby the synergies to be extracted from a multi-sectoral approach can have maximum impact on the lives of individuals at the community level.
The Project will continue its activities implementation in Donetsk and Luhansk oblasts as soon as the territories are liberated and the security situation allows. So far, in the nearest future it seems to be unlike scenario.
The activities support the displaced and war-affected populations and institutions and prepare a ground for their gradual return to their home areas in the east of Ukraine. For instance, the original orientation of the capacitating of local civil and military administrations has become more relevant to the new war-affected areas, such as Chernihiv, Dnipropetrovsk, Mykolaiv and Sumy oblasts. UNDPs expertise in supporting the implementation of capacity-development events on good governance will be widely disseminated. Horizontal assistance for service provision and environmental protection in the selected target areas under the project will be complemented by and integrated with vertical assistance from local components of UNDPs national projects and programmes, as well as coordinated with the work of other UN Agencies and implementing partners. For instance, the initial orientation to capacitate local civil and military administrations in Donetsk and Luhansk oblasts has also become relevant to the other war-affected and IDP-hosting oblasts such as Chernihiv, Dnipropetrovsk, Mykolaiv and Sumy oblasts.
In particular, at the first stage, the Project had capacitated the local authorities regarding labour relations, rights and obligations of employers and employees under martial law; grounds for dismissal of an employee; grounds for terminating the employment contract; settlement of issues of payment or additional leave to certain social groups, including IDPs, persons with disabilities and other war-affected populations.
Moreover, the Project provided training sessions to the local authorities of the host communities, including from the west of Ukraine, on delivering quality gender-responsive social services at the local level, focusing on those population groups directly affected by the war.
